about.title: About Chicago Public Schools
about.content: Chicago Public Schools, also known as CPS, serves students across Chicago, Illinois. The CPS calendar is useful for tracking the K-12 first day, preschool start date, holidays, professional development days, parent-teacher conference days, winter vacation, spring vacation, quarter endings, report-card distribution dates, and the last day of school.

about.title: How to Use This CPS Calendar
about.content: Use this page for districtwide elementary and high school calendar planning. Families should still confirm school-specific bell schedules, local events, graduation ceremonies, summer programs, athletics, testing, and emergency schedule changes through CPS and their assigned school.

planningTips.title: Planning Tips for CPS Families
content: Track professional development days separately because CPS lists them as non-attendance days for students.
Parent-teacher conference days after the first and third quarters are student non-attendance days for elementary and high schools.
Preschool dates differ from K-12 dates, so families with younger children should check the preschool start and end dates.
Emergency days in June may become school days if required to meet state attendance requirements.

customSections.label: About CPS Calendar Structure
customSections.content: The CPS calendar is built around a districtwide traditional calendar for most elementary and high school students, but the official family calendars include details that matter specifically in Chicago. CPS separates K-12 and preschool first and last days, identifies parent-teacher conference days as student non-attendance days, and marks professional development days that can affect childcare and transportation. The calendar also lists quarter endings, progress report dates, report card distribution dates, graduation windows, and anticipated summer program timing. For 2026-2027, CPS publishes translated family calendars in Arabic, Polish, Simplified Chinese, Ukrainian, Urdu, and Vietnamese, which is important for families comparing the same school-year dates across languages. Emergency days are also part of the CPS calendar structure, so the June schedule should be verified before final travel or summer plans.

customSections.label: Chicago Public Schools Calendar Planning Notes
customSections.content: The Chicago Public Schools calendar includes several planning details beyond major holidays. The CPS family calendar PDFs identify K-12 dates separately from preschool dates, mark professional development days, show parent-teacher conference days as student non-attendance days, list report and progress report distribution dates, and reserve emergency days in June if student days fall below state requirements.

customSections.label: CPS Calendar vs School-Specific Calendars
customSections.content: The district CPS calendar is the right source for systemwide dates such as the first day of school, winter vacation, spring vacation, parent-teacher conference days, and district holidays. It does not always include school-specific events, athletics, testing schedules, local ceremonies, transportation changes, or program calendars. Families should use the Chicago Public Schools calendar for districtwide planning and then confirm campus-level details with their assigned school.

customSections.label: How We Collect CPS Calendar Data
customSections.content: MySchoolDates reviews the official CPS family calendar and extracts student dates, holidays, breaks, parent-teacher conference days, professional development days, and other planning dates. The page links back to the official Chicago Public Schools source so families can verify updates before making final childcare, travel, transportation, or work plans.

districtFaqs.q: Which Chicago Public Schools calendar does this page summarize?
districtFaqs.a: This page summarizes the official CPS Family Calendar for elementary and high schools for the listed school years.

districtFaqs.q: Does CPS list preschool dates separately?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. CPS family calendars list K-12 first and last days separately from preschool first and last days.

districtFaqs.q: Are CPS parent-teacher conference days student attendance days?
districtFaqs.a: No. CPS states that elementary and high school parent-teacher conference days are non-attendance days for students.

districtFaqs.q: Where should families verify Chicago Public Schools calendar updates?
districtFaqs.a: Use the official CPS calendar page and school announcements for final confirmation. MySchoolDates is an independent reference and is not affiliated with Chicago Public Schools.

districtFaqs.q: Are CPS calendar dates the same for every school?
districtFaqs.a: Not always. The CPS family calendar covers districtwide elementary and high school dates, but individual schools may publish separate events, testing dates, athletics schedules, graduation details, or program-specific calendars.

districtFaqs.q: What calendar does CPS use for most students?
districtFaqs.a: Most CPS students follow the districtwide traditional family calendar for elementary and high schools, while some programs or schools may publish additional school-specific schedules.

districtFaqs.q: Does CPS have a calendar for charter schools?
districtFaqs.a: Charter schools may follow separate calendars or publish school-specific schedule details. Families should verify charter school dates directly with the school in addition to checking CPS districtwide calendar information.
